text:
Aisha: ugh...my Wi‑Fi dies every day at ~3pm.
Aisha: tracked it down to neighbor's new "smart sprinkler" — it's blasting 2.4GHz on the same channel. :facepalm: pic: (sprinkler-router.jpg)
Tom: wait what, a sprinkler using Wi‑Fi? post pic pls
Priya: 2.4GHz IoT devices suck. can you move your AP to a different channel or force 5GHz band steering?
Marco: can you do an `iwlist` scan and paste output? sometimes microwave/door openers also jump in
RouterBot: [auto] WAN link flapping detected at 15:03 UTC — events: 6
Aisha: here's the scan around 14:58, you can see a big 2.4GHz SSID on ch6 every day at 3pm
```
Cell 01 - Address: AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF
Channel:6
ESSID:"backyard-sprinkler"
Signal level=-42 dBm
```
Riley: omg backyard-sprinkler is a top-tier SSID name
Priya: try forcing channel 1 or 11, or set your AP to prefer 5GHz. also check client devices — some will stubbornly drop to 2.4.
Tom: temporary: tether phone to 5G for meetings or run a long Ethernet to window/balcony
Marco: if you want, I can lend a cheap travel AP (supports 5GHz only) for a few days
Aisha: thanks y'all. Ordered a 5GHz mesh node and scheduled a test at 3pm today. Will report back with victory or defeat :crossed_fingers:
